category_title: At-risk four-year-olds from low-income families with context-dependent oral language proficiency
scenario_title: Oral language engagement during teaching-directed storybook reading
minimal_context: The student is answering questions about a storybook during a teaching-directed reading activity.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's read this storybook together. Look at this picture here. What animal is this?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Yes, it's a bear. What color is the bear?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Right. And what is the bear eating?

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Let's read this storybook together. Look at this picture here. What animal is this?

STUDENT: Bear.

TUTOR: Yes, it's a bear. What color is the bear?

STUDENT: Brown.

TUTOR: Right. And what is the bear eating?

STUDENT: (Pauses and looks down hesitantly) Fish.

task.content: Engaging in oral language during teaching-directed experiences
task.learning_goal: Develop the language and literacy skills necessary for school success

context.social_setting: Speaking to an adult (teacher and/or paraprofessional)

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When adults were asking predominantly low level questions and accepting one word responses or phrases
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Employed more undesired language usage; used one word responses or phrases
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Hesitant to use more elaborate language due to the fear of making grammatical errors

behavior_patterns.condition: When speaking to an adult during teaching directed experiences
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Demonstrated desired language usage less than one-third of the time (an average of 31.6 % of the time)
Used one word responses 28.8% of the time, phrases 15.4% of the time
